hints: Without the fee you would grab every small upswing. With a fee, tiny wiggles are no longer worth a round trip — so you need to remember whether you are currently holding a share, not just look at neighbouring days.
Two-state DP: free = best profit not holding a share, hold = best profit while holding. Charge the fee once per round trip, when you sell.

1. Start: free = 0, hold = -prices[0].
  2. For each later price p:
  3. newFree = max(free, hold + p - fee) (sell today and pay the fee).
  4. newHold = max(hold, free - p) (buy today).
  5. Return free at the end.

approaches.name: Brute force
approaches.idea: Recursively try buy / sell / wait every day.

approaches.name: Optimal
approaches.idea: Hold / free state DP with O(1) memory.

explain: For [1, 4, 2, 9, 3, 7] with fee 2: buying at 1 and selling at 9 earns 8 − 2 = 6, then buying at 3 and selling at 7 earns 4 − 2 = 2, total 8. The DP discovers this because hold keeps the cheapest effective buy, and free only changes when a sale beats doing nothing after the fee. When the fee eats the whole gain, like [3, 5] with fee 3, the answer stays 0.
recognize: 'Unlimited trades but each trade costs a fee' → hold/free stock DP subtracting the fee on sell.
